answer.rationale: Current situation shows simultaneous decline in activation (6% QoQ) and onboarding completion (4% QoQ), with competitive pressure on price-sensitive SMBs. Memory_91 demonstrates that activation messaging improved week-one engagement and first meaningful action—directly addressing the activation decline. Memory_31 showed signup simplification worked for SMB activation. Memory_86 established that shortened onboarding lifted adoption. However, activation messaging targets the engagement phase post-onboarding, which is the most immediate leverage point for the 6% activation drop. Verifying memory_91 and memory_31 will confirm effect durability and interaction patterns. Promotional pricing (memory_73) would address competitor pressure but risks margin and doesn't solve the activation/onboarding completion metrics decline. Referral incentives (memory_57) work in established customers, not in acquisition scenarios. Enterprise sales assist (memory_44) is orthogonal to SMB activation crisis. A standard experiment on activation messaging targets the core problem with proven mechanism and preserves option value on pricing response if needed next week.
